clue.text: A fighter, maybe, but not against change

indicators.note: the instruction to change tells us to rearrange the two words before it into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier, perhaps, though not one who resists change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges NOT AGAINST into the answer; 'but' just links. 'maybe' warns that a fighter is only one kind of opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent or adversary in a contest may well be a fighter, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Cunning at bridge?

explanation.surface: Someone is crafty at the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' suggests the card game but means the curved span; 'at' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means sly or roguish, as in an arch look; it is also the curved span of a bridge.

clue.text: Book coming my way

parts.note: coming towards somewhere is going to it
my way here means towards me, the speaker

explanation.surface: A volume is on its way to me in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: Something coming my way is coming to me, so the pieces read TO ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a large, heavy volume.

clue.text: Traveller going round in circles?

parts.note: suggests a lost wanderer, but the circles are those of the earth, round which a tourist travels

explanation.surface: A lost wayfarer who keeps returning to the same spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist who travels widely round the world, the round earth being the 'circle'.

clue.text: What we hear spread abroad by rumour

explanation.surface: Gossip passed around until everyone has heard it.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'noise abroad' is an old phrase for spreading a report about.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is sound heard; as a verb, to noise something abroad is to circulate it as gossip.

clue.text: This zone should be clearly defined

definitions.text: This zone should be clearly defined

parts.words: This zone should be clearly defined
parts.note: 'clearly' suggests well marked, but means with clean air, free of coal smoke

explanation.surface: A planner insists the boundaries of an area be marked plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: British Clean Air Acts set up zones where only fuel that burns without fumes may be used, so the air there is clear.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone where only fuels producing no fumes may be burned, keeping the air clean.

clue.text: Shows it's not only the best who come out on top

definitions.text: Shows it's not only the best who come out on top

parts.words: Shows it's not only the best who come out on top
parts.note: the frothy dirt on a liquid floats to the surface, so the worst of things also rises to the top

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that success does not always go to the most deserving.
explanation.definitionFit: Froth or dirt rising to the top of a liquid, and figuratively worthless people, proves the worst also reach the top.

clue.text: Accidental troops

explanation.surface: Soldiers who arrived by chance.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means dependent on chance, and also a body of troops sent as part of a larger force.

clue.text: His complaints don't merit investigation

parts.note: his 'complaints' are illnesses he pretends to have, so a doctor need not look into them

explanation.surface: Someone's grievances are not worth looking into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaints' reads as grievances but means ailments, which this shirker only feigns.
explanation.definitionFit: A shirker who feigns illness to avoid work has ailments that need no doctor's examination.

clue.text: The right type needed for this job

definitions.text: The right type needed for this job

parts.words: The right type needed for this job
parts.note: 'type' means printing type, which a typesetter must pick and arrange correctly, not the right kind of person

explanation.surface: A recruiter says only a suitable kind of person will do for the post.
explanation.definitionFit: A typesetter arranges printing type by hand, so the right type is literally the job.

clue.text: A love of indigo

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, so nil

explanation.surface: Someone confesses a fondness for the colour indigo.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis 'love' means a score of zero, giving NIL; 'of' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is a West Indian shrub and the blue dye made from it, the plant source of indigo.

clue.text: Treatment for a shock, perhaps

parts.note: a shock can be a thick mass of hair, which is cut and styled rather than treated medically

explanation.surface: First aid for someone who has had a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting and styling at a salon is what a thick bushy head of hair gets.

clue.text: Rate reduction?

parts.note: reads like a cut in local taxes or interest, but means a fall in speed

explanation.surface: A headline asking whether a tax or interest rate will be cut.
explanation.walkthrough: British 'rates' were local property taxes, which is where the surface points; here the rate is speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Slowing down is a reduction in the rate of motion, i.e. in velocity.

clue.text: Practical details of a capital levy, say?

parts.note: brass is slang for money, i.e. capital

indicators.note: say tells us the word for levy is spoken, and its sound-alike is written

parts.note: a tax is a levy

explanation.surface: Asking about the specifics of a tax on wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' is northern English slang for money; 'of a' links. 'getting down to' these means facing basic facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic facts and essentials, as in getting down to the nitty-gritty.

clue.text: Example of initial confusion, in a manner of speaking

definitions.text: Example of initial confusion, in a manner of speaking

parts.words: Example of initial confusion, in a manner of speaking
parts.note: the confusion is of the first letters of words in speech, swapped by mistake, as Reverend Spooner famously did

explanation.surface: A remark about muddled beginnings, figuratively speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip of the tongue swapping the opening sounds of two words, named after Oxford don William Spooner.

clue.text: About a story with a moral that can be put right

parts.note: re is a short word meaning about or concerning
a parable is a simple story told to teach a moral lesson

explanation.surface: Concerning a fable whose lesson can be corrected.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repairable or mendable is capable of being put right.

clue.text: Bearer of papers should not long detain the court

definitions.text: should not long detain the court

explanation.surface: A lawyer's bag and a quick hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Split, the two words mean a short lawsuit; joined, a flat bag for documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat bag carries documents; split, the words mean a short lawsuit that a judge would finish quickly.

clue.text: Herries an unprincipled fellow?

parts.note: names the title of Hugh Walpole's 1930 novel about Francis Herries, whose first word means a scoundrel

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man called Herries is a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Hugh Walpole's novel 'Rogue Herries' (1930) is about a wayward Cumberland squire; the missing first word of the title is also a word for a rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal or scoundrel is an unprincipled man, and the word also begins Walpole's novel title.

clue.text: Not the slimmer's drink?

parts.note: the drink is a dark beer whose name also means fat, the opposite of slim

explanation.surface: A dieter is told which drink to avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong dark porter-style beer shares its name with the word for portly, so no dieter would choose it.

clue.text: Run, in case there's trouble, for cover

indicators.note: trouble here means disorder among the letters of the words before it, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to flee, just in case danger arises, and take shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's trouble' rearranges RUN and IN CASE (RUNINCASE) into the answer; 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy giving financial protection against loss is called cover.

clue.text: But old enough to be the scene of the Red King's death

definitions.text: But old enough to be the scene of the Red King's death

parts.words: But old enough to be the scene of the Red King's death
parts.note: William II, nicknamed Rufus (the Red King), was killed hunting in a Hampshire forest in 1100, though its name calls it new

explanation.surface: A history note on where a medieval king died.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red King is William Rufus, shot by an arrow while hunting in 1100 in a royal forest in Hampshire, England; 'But old' jokes that its name says it is new.
explanation.definitionFit: This Hampshire forest, created by William the Conqueror, is where William Rufus was killed in 1100.

clue.text: Trees put in a different formation

indicators.note: the letters of trees are arranged in a new formation, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener replants a group of trees in a new pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a different formation' rearranges TREES; the answer means set or put again.
explanation.definitionFit: To set again is to put back in place, set being a synonym of the verb place.

clue.text: Singer cager for a rise

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise means reading upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: avid means keen or eager

explanation.surface: A vocalist longs for a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a rise' in a down clue turns AVID upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera vocalist.

clue.text: The giant in Pilgrim's Progress

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the letters of the title that follows

explanation.surface: A reference to Giant Despair in Bunyan's allegory.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface brings Giant Despair to mind, but 'in' signals the answer sitting inside the second word of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a monstrous giant of folk tales.

clue.text: It's fashionable to have a go in America

definitions.text: It's fashionable to have a go in America

parts.words: It's fashionable to have a go in America
parts.note: a word for stylish, given the letters of 'a go' after it, becomes a big American city

explanation.surface: Trying something out is in vogue in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer means fashionable; add A GO and you get CHICAGO, a city in America. 'have a go' looks like 'make an attempt' but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish, smart and fashionable.

clue.text: The mariner - (3,7), enjoying a carouse

explanation.surface: An old sailor, at sea and drinking merrily.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 3,7 the answer completes 'The mariner ... ' as two words about being at sea; run together it is one word for drinking festively.
explanation.definitionFit: Two words saying the sailor was at sea; one word meaning toasting and drinking merrily at a festive revel.

clue.text: Not the whole amount, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for amount is only heard, and a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: a sum is an amount, as of money

explanation.surface: Someone reports hearing that it was not the full amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A part or a portion, less than all of something, is what the definition describes.

clue.text: Madly reading etc for degrees in this

indicators.note: madly tells us the letters of the next two words go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone frantically studying et cetera to earn university degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madly' rearranges READING ETC into the answer; 'for' links. The 'degrees' are of temperature, not university ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperature can be measured in degrees on the Celsius scale, a hundred-step scale.
